'''''Eustoma exaltatum''''', commonly called '''seaside gentian''',<ref name=IRC>[https://www.regionalconservation.org/beta/nfyn/plantdetail.asp?tx=Eustexal Seaside gentian] The Institute for Regional Conservation</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family ([[Gentianaceae]]). 

==Description==
''Eustoma exaltatum'' is an erect herbaceous plant with a glaucous, leafy stem. It produces large, purple, bell-shaped flowers throughout the growing season, peaking in spring through summer.<ref name=AZ/><ref name=IRC/>

''[[Eustoma russellianum]]'' is closely related to ''Eustoma exaltatum'', and in some treatments they are ranked as subspecies, rather than as separate species.<ref name=Jepson/>

==Distribution==
It is native to North America, where it found in from the southern [[United States]] and the [[West Indies]], south to [[Mexico]] and [[Belize]].<ref name=Weakley>{{cite web |url=http://www.herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |title= Flora of the Southern and Mid-Atlantic States |author= Alan Weakley |date= 2015}}</ref> Its natural habitat is wet places, such as alkaline marshes, stream beds, and saline coastal areas.<ref name=Weakley/><ref name=Jepson>[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=80520 ''Eustoma exaltatum'' subsp. ''exaltatum''] The Jepson Herbarium</ref><ref name=AZ>{{cite book |last1=Kearney |first1=Thomas |last2=Peebles |first2=Robert |date=1942 |title=Flowering plants and ferns of Arizona |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/132362 |location= |publisher=[[U.S. Dept. of Agriculture]] |page=861 |isbn= |author-link= }}</ref> It is moderately tolerant of inundation by salt water, and highly tolerant of salt winds.<ref name=IRC/>
